derivations.claim: Before any Toffoli gate, $r=0$, which is the empty parity $p_0$.

If after processing coordinates $0,\ldots,i-1$ the work bit is $p_i=\bigoplus_{j<i}(a_j\land x_j)$, the next Toffoli leaves the controls unchanged and changes $r$ to $p_i\oplus(a_i\land x_i)=p_{i+1}$ by [F3]. Thus the forward invariant holds for every $i\le n$.
At the end of the forward loop, $r=p_n=a\cdot x$ by [F2]. This includes $n=0$, for which step 1.1 is already the final state.
The CNOT now changes $z$ to $z\oplus r=z\oplus(a\cdot x)$ and leaves $a,x,r$ unchanged by [F4].

In the reverse loop, define $q_i$ to be the accumulator after the gates for coordinates $n-1,n-2,\ldots,i$ have been applied. Before any reverse gate, $q_n=p_n$. If $q_{i+1}=p_{i+1}$, the next Toffoli toggles $q_{i+1}$ by $a_i\land x_i$, so $q_i=p_{i+1}\oplus(a_i\land x_i)=p_i$. Descending through $i=n-1,\ldots,0$ therefore ends at $q_0=p_0=0$. The reverse gates do not change $a,x,z$, so the work bit is clean.

The input basis map is the claimed map by steps 3.1 and 4.1. Every gate is linear, and the computational basis spans the finite register by [F6], so the same identity holds on every superposition. The forward and reverse loops each have $n$ Toffoli occurrences and there is one CNOT, giving the exact stated cost and no branch in the algorithm.

derivations.claim: On each computational-basis input $|x\rangle|y\rangle$, the defined action leaves $x$ fixed and changes $y$ to $y\oplus f(x)$. Applying it twice changes the target to $(y\oplus f(x))\oplus f(x)=y$, since each bit toggled twice returns to its original value. Hence the action is involutive on every basis vector.

Let $C=Q_2=\mathbb C^2$ be the control qubit with ordered computational basis $|0\rangle,|1\rangle$; define $|\pm\rangle=(|0\rangle\pm|1\rangle)/\sqrt2$ and prepare $(|0\rangle+\overline\mu|1\rangle)/\sqrt2$ with target $\phi$. The two joint effects are $E_\pm=|\pm\rangle\langle\pm|\otimes I_H$. The $E_+$ outcome has probability $1$ after $C(U)$ and $\cos^2(\theta/2)$ after $C(e^{i\theta}U)$. Thus the two controlled maps give different outcome laws exactly when $\theta\notin2\pi\mathbb Z$; when $\theta\in2\pi\mathbb Z$, the controlled maps coincide. This is a mathematical witness; it does not assert that controlled access or the witness-state preparation is free.

derivations.claim: Since $f(x)=c$ for every address $x$, [F1] gives $P_f|x\rangle=(-1)^c|x\rangle$ on a basis; hence $P_f=(-1)^cI$.

Under [A1], the controlled block is $I$ if $c=0$. If $c=1$, it is $\operatorname{diag}(I,-I)$ by [F3]. Applying these blocks to $|+\rangle|0^a\rangle$ gives respectively $|+\rangle|0^a\rangle$ and $(|0\rangle-|1\rangle)|0^a\rangle/\sqrt2=|-\rangle|0^a\rangle$. This is the $\theta=\pi$, $U=I$ relative-phase instance of [F6]; the controlled identity is the identity operation and the other block is the explicitly granted controlled phase call.

The scalar has modulus one. Applying [F2] to any normalized address state shows that the standalone call preserves every finite POVM outcome law. This verifies the statement even when $c=1$ and the vector acquires a minus sign.

The explicit vectors $|+\rangle=(|0\rangle+|1\rangle)/\sqrt2$ and $|-\rangle=(|0\rangle-|1\rangle)/\sqrt2$ have unit norm and inner product zero by [F5]. The two control outputs therefore give opposite deterministic outcomes when measured in that basis, proving distinguishability. The proof uses the explicitly controlled operation [A1] and makes no claim from uncontrolled access alone.

derivations.claim: Let the one-bit address be $x$ and the target be $y$. The first CNOT from $x$ to clean work $r$ maps $|x\rangle|0\rangle_r$ to $|x\rangle|x\rangle_r$ by [F9]. Copying $r$ to $y$ changes $y$ to $y\oplus x$. The final CNOT from $x$ to $r$ restores $r$ to $x\oplus x=0$ and leaves $x,y\oplus x$ unchanged. Thus the three-CNOT circuit is exactly the standard query for $f(x)=x$ with clean work.

For $a=11$ and $x=10$, the two coordinate products are $1\land1=1$ and $1\land0=0$, so $a\cdot x=1\oplus0=1$ by [F4]. In the forward Toffoli loop of [F5], the first gate changes $r:0\to1$ and the second leaves it at $1$; CNOT changes $z:0\to1$. In reverse, the second Toffoli leaves $r$ unchanged and the first changes $r:1\to0$ by [F8]. Thus the output is $|11\rangle|10\rangle|1\rangle|0\rangle_r$, consistent with [F6].

Starting with address $|+\rangle$, target $|-\rangle$, and clean work $|0\rangle_r$, step 1.1 applies the standard query. By [F3] the output is $|-\rangle_x|-\rangle_y|0\rangle_r$. Multiplying the matrix in [F10] gives $H|0\rangle=|+\rangle$ and $H|1\rangle=|-\rangle$, hence $H|-\rangle=|1\rangle$. The final address measurement therefore returns $1$ with probability one.

Omit only the final CNOT from $x$ to $r$ in step 1.1. After compute and copy, the input $|+\rangle_x|-\rangle_y|0\rangle_r$ is
$$
\frac{|0\rangle_x|0\rangle_r-|1\rangle_x|1\rangle_r}{\sqrt2}\otimes|-\rangle_y
$$
Applying $H$ to the address gives
$$
\frac{|0\rangle_x|-\rangle_r+|1\rangle_x|+\rangle_r}{\sqrt2}\otimes|-\rangle_y
$$
Because $|+\rangle_r$ and $|-\rangle_r$ are orthogonal unit vectors, address outcomes $0$ and $1$ each have probability $1/2$. The residual work value is correlated with the address, violating the clean-ancilla contract [F7] and destroying the intended deterministic interference.

For the constant function $f(x)=1$, [F2] gives $P_f=-I$, a standalone global scalar; [F12] therefore gives no standalone measurement distinction from $I$. Under the explicit controlled call, the control output is $|+\rangle$ for the identity case and $|-\rangle$ for the constant-one case by [F12]. Matrix multiplication using [F10] gives $H|+\rangle=|0\rangle$ and $H|-\rangle=|1\rangle$, so a computational-basis measurement distinguishes them with certainty.
